distractors.why: Numerators x+2 and x+4 are added without being multiplied by 3 and 2, then put over the common denominator 6. This gives 2x+6 over 6, which is exactly the numerator-not-scaled error. It is not equal to (5x+14)/6.
Adds numerators (x+2)+(x+4)=2x+6 and denominators 2+3=5. This is exactly the add-across error. It is wrong.
The factor multiplies only the first term of each bracket: 3(x+2) becomes 3x+2 and 2(x+4) becomes 2x+4. The sum is 5x+6. This is exactly the missing-distribution error, and it is wrong.
Numerators x+2 and x+5 add to 2x+7 and denominators 3+7 add to 10. This is exactly the add-across error. It is wrong.
Numerators are added unscaled (2x+7) over the common denominator 21. This is exactly the numerator-not-scaled error. It is not equal to (10x+29)/21.
7(x+2) becomes 7x+2 and 3(x+5) becomes 3x+5, giving 10x+7. This is exactly the missing-distribution error, and it is wrong.
Numerators x+1 and x+3 add to 2x+4 and denominators 5+7 add to 12. This is exactly the add-across error. It is wrong.
Numerators are added unscaled (2x+4) over the common denominator 35. This is exactly the numerator-not-scaled error. It is not equal to (12x+22)/35.
7(x+1) becomes 7x+1 and 5(x+3) becomes 5x+3, giving 12x+4. This is exactly the missing-distribution error, and it is wrong.
